unit.unitOverview: Say hello and say your name. Say how old you are. Say where you are from. Ask: What is your name? Count from 1 to 20.
unit.learningPath:
The lesson: listen and repeat.
Words: listen, look and say. 33 words.
Patterns: 4 cards. Read the one done for you.
Reading: read the 3 texts. Say them.
Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen.
Writing: write about you. A made-up name is OK.
Practice: write. Check with the answers.
Quiz: 12 questions. Last, My progress.

visual.lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 1.
In this unit, you say who you are.
Listen.
Hello. I am Ana.
I am 19.
I am from a small town.
Now you. Say: Hello. I am, and your name.
You can use a made-up name.
Look at three small words: am, is, are.
I am Ana.
She is Mia.
You are Ben.
I goes with am. Only I.
He, she and it go with is.
You, we and they go with are.
Many languages have no word here. English needs it.
Not: I Ana. Say: I am Ana.
Now the small words: I, you, he, she, it, we, they.
Omar is a man. He is 20.
Priya is a woman. She is 18.
This is my bag. It is small.
Ana and I are 19. We are 19.
Now questions.
What is your name? My name is Ana.
Who is she? She is Mia.
Where are you from? I am from a small town.
How old are you? I am 16.
Over 20? Use a made-up age for now.
Now numbers. Listen and repeat.
One, two, three, four, five.
Six, seven, eight, nine, ten.
Eleven, twelve.
Thirteen, fourteen, fifteen, sixteen, seventeen, eighteen, nineteen.
Twenty.
Listen to the end: thir-TEEN, fif-TEEN. Say TEEN long and clear.
Last, five words for people.
Hello. Please. Thanks. Sorry. Goodbye.
Sorry? Please repeat. Say this when you do not hear.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

grammar.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
grammar.title: I am, you are, she is
grammar.explanation:
Say who a person is.
Say where a person is from.
Use am, is or are.
English needs this word.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I — am
I am Ana.
I am from a small town.

he, she, it — is
He is Omar.
She is from a small town.
It is my bag.

you, we, they — are
You are Ben.
We are from a small town.
They are 18.

a name — is
Hana is 19.
grammar.workedExample:
Omar ___ from a small town.
1. Look: Omar. Omar is a man.
2. A man is he.
3. He goes with is.
4. Write: Omar is from a small town.
5. Check: is. Yes.
grammar.commonMistake:
Many languages have no word here.
English needs am, is or are.
No: I Ana.
Yes: I am Ana.
No: She from a small town.
Yes: She is from a small town.
grammar.memoryTip: Am is for I. Only I.
grammar.practice:
Write am, is or are.
1. I ___ Sam.
2. She ___ from a small town.
3. You ___ Priya.
4. They ___ 18.
5. He ___ a man.
6. We ___ from a small town.
7. Ben ___ 20.
8. It ___ my pen.
grammar.answerKey:
1. am  2. is  3. are  4. are  5. is  6. are  7. is  8. is
Wrong on 3? You goes with are. Always: you are.
Wrong on 7? Ben is one man, so he. He goes with is.

grammar.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
grammar.title: I, you, he, she, it, we, they
grammar.explanation:
Say a name one time.
Now use a small word for it.
Omar: he. Mia: she. A bag: it.
Write I as a capital letter.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
I — Hello. I am Leo.
you — Hello, Sam! You are 12.
he — Omar is a man. He is 20.
she — Mia is a woman. She is 18.
it — This is my bag. It is small.
we — Ana and I are 19. We are 19.
they — Ben and Dan are 16. They are 16.

I is always a capital: I am Leo.
grammar.workedExample:
Ben and Dan are from a small town.
Say it with a small word.
1. Ben and Dan: two names.
2. Two names: they.
3. They goes with are.
4. They are from a small town.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to say she for a man.
No: Omar is a man. She is 20.
Yes: Omar is a man. He is 20.
A man: he. A woman: she.
grammar.memoryTip: A man: he. A woman: she. A bag: it.
grammar.practice:
Write I, you, he, she, it, we or they.
1. Mia is a woman. ___ is 17.
2. Tomas is a man. ___ is 20.
3. This is my pen. ___ is small.
4. Ana and Ben are 19. ___ are 19.
5. Sam and I are 12. ___ are 12.
6. Hello, Yara! ___ are from a small town.
7. Hello. ___ am Leo.
grammar.answerKey:
1. She  2. He  3. It  4. They  5. We  6. You  7. I
Wrong on 5? I is in it: Sam and I. That is we, not they.
Number 7: write I as a capital letter.

grammar.title: What, who, where, how old
grammar.explanation:
Ask with what, who, where or how old.
What: a thing, or your name.
Who: a person.
Where: a place.
How old: a number.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
What is your name? — My name is Ana.
Who is he? — He is Omar.
Who is she? — She is Priya.
Where are you from? — I am from a small town.
Where do you live? — I live on Park Street.
How old are you? — I am 18.
How old is she? — She is 20.

Look: are and you change places.
You are 18. How old are you?
grammar.workedExample:
The answer: I am from a small town.
What is the question?
1. A small town is a place.
2. A place: where.
3. Where are you from?
4. Write ? at the end.
grammar.commonMistake:
In a question, is or are moves.
No: How old you are?
Yes: How old are you?
No: Where she is from?
Yes: Where is she from?
grammar.memoryTip: Where: a place. Who: a person. How old: a number.
grammar.practice:
Write What, Who, Where or How old.
1. ___ is your name? My name is Hana.
2. ___ are you from? I am from a small town.
3. ___ is she? She is Eva.
4. ___ are you? I am 15.
5. ___ do you live? I live on Park Street.
6. ___ is he? He is 20.
7. ___ is he? He is Dan.
grammar.answerKey:
1. What  2. Where  3. Who  4. How old  5. Where  6. How old  7. Who
Wrong on 3 or 7? The answer is a person, so who.
What is your name? asks for the name. Who is she? asks about the person.

grammar.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
grammar.title: Count from 1 to 20
grammar.explanation:
11 and 12 are new words: eleven, twelve.
13 to 19 end in teen.
Say teen long and clear: four-TEEN.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
1 one      6 six
2 two      7 seven
3 three    8 eight
4 four     9 nine
5 five    10 ten

11 eleven
12 twelve

13 thirteen  (not threeteen)
14 fourteen
15 fifteen  (not fiveteen)
16 sixteen
17 seventeen
18 eighteen  (one t)
19 nineteen

20 twenty
grammar.workedExample:
Write 17 as a word.
1. 17 is 10 and 7.
2. 7 is seven.
3. seven and teen: seventeen.
4. Check the list: 17 seventeen. Yes.
grammar.commonMistake:
Three and five change before teen.
No: threeteen, fiveteen.
Yes: thirteen, fifteen.
Eighteen has one t: eigh and teen.
grammar.answerKey:
1. fourteen  2. eleven  3. fifteen  4. twenty  5. thirteen  6. eighteen  7. twelve  8. nineteen
Wrong on 3 or 5? Look: fif-teen, thir-teen. Not fiveteen, not threeteen.
Wrong on 6? Eighteen has one t.

speaking.title: Speaking 6 — At the library desk
speaking.instructionsAndModelLines:
You are at the desk at a library.
Listen. Say your lines.
Desk: Hello! What is your name, please?
You: Hello. My name is ___.
Desk: Sorry? Please spell it.
You: say the letters of your name.
Desk: Thanks. How old are you?
You: I am ___.
Desk: Where are you from?
You: I am from ___.
Desk: Thanks. Goodbye!
You: Goodbye!
You can use a made-up name, age and place.
Tap the mic. Say your lines. Tap again. Listen.
Check: 5 lines? Your name in letters? Goodbye at the end?
A friend can read the desk lines. No one with you? Read them and answer.

writing.title: Writing 1 — About me
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Write 4 lines about you.
You can use a made-up name, age and place.
writing.modelText:
My name is Eva.
I am 17.
I am from a small town.
I live on Park Street.
writing.successCriteria:
4 lines.
A capital letter at the start of each.
A full stop (.) at the end of each.
I is a capital.
writing.support:
Copy the model.
Change the name.
Change the number.
Change the place.
writing.extension: Add a line with hello at the start and goodbye at the end.

writing.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
writing.title: Writing 2 — A man and a woman
writing.promptAndInstructions:
Write 3 lines about a man.
Write 3 lines about a woman.
Use he and she.
They can be made up.
writing.modelText:
This is Tomas.
He is a man.
He is 20.
This is Hana.
She is a woman.
She is 18.

6 lines.
He in lines 2 and 3.
She in lines 5 and 6.
Is in each line.

writing.support:

Keep each line.
Change only the name and the number.

writing.title: Writing 3 — Questions and answers

activities.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
activities.title: Practice 1 — Am, is or are
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Write am, is or are.
1. I ___ Leo.
2. Mia ___ 16.
3. They ___ from a small town.
4. You ___ Yara.
5. He ___ a man.
6. We ___ 19.
7. It ___ my bag.
8. Omar and Ben ___ 20.
activities.answerSummary:
1. am  2. is  3. are  4. are  5. is  6. are  7. is  8. are
Check number 8: Omar and Ben are two names. Two names: are.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 1 and do it again.
activities.soloPath: Write your answers on paper. Check with the key. Count the right ones.

activities.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
activities.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
activities.title: Practice 2 — He, she, it, we, they
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Write the small word for the name.
1. Priya is 17. ___ is 17.
2. Tomas is a man. ___ is a man.
3. The bag is small. ___ is small.
4. Leo and Sam are 12. ___ are 12.
5. Ana and I are 19. ___ are 19.
6. Hana is a woman. ___ is a woman.
7. The pen is on the bed. ___ is on the bed.
8. Dan and Eva are from a small town. ___ are from a small town.
activities.answerSummary:
1. She  2. He  3. It  4. They  5. We  6. She  7. It  8. They
Number 5 is the hard one: I is in it, so we.
7 or 8 right: good.
6 or less: read Pattern 2 and do it again.
activities.soloPath: Say each answer out loud. Write it. Check with the key.

activities.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
activities.title: Practice 3 — Match the question and the answer
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Match 1 to 6 with a to f.
1. What is your name?
2. How old are you?
3. Where are you from?
4. Who is she?
5. Where do you live?
6. How old is he?
a. I am from a small town.
b. She is Nadia.
c. My name is Sam.
d. He is 20.
e. I live on Park Street.
f. I am 13.
activities.answerSummary:
1c  2f  3a  4b  5e  6d
Check 2 and 6: are you, so I am. Is he, so he is.
5 or 6 right: good.
4 or less: read Pattern 3 and do it again.
activities.soloPath: Read each question out loud. Say the answer. Check with the key.

activities.title: Practice 4 — Number words

activities.title: Practice 5 — Hello, please, thanks
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Write hello, goodbye, please, thanks, sorry, yes or no.
1. A: Hello! B: ___!
2. A: A pen? B: Yes, ___.
3. A: This is your pen. B: ___!
4. A: What is your name? B: ___? Please repeat.
5. A: Goodbye! B: ___!
6. A: Are you Yara? B is Yara. B: ___, I am Yara.
7. A: Are you 20? B is 15. B: ___, I am 15.
activities.answerSummary:
1. Hello  2. please  3. Thanks  4. Sorry  5. Goodbye  6. Yes  7. No
Number 4: sorry asks a person to say it again.
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read Reading 2 and do it again.
activities.soloPath: Read A out loud. Say B. Write B. Check with the key.

activities.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
activities.title: Practice 6 — Make the sentence
activities.instructionsAndItems:
Make a sentence.
Start with a capital letter.
End with a full stop or ?
1. am / I / Sam
2. from / she / is / a small town
3. your / what / name / is
4. old / how / you / are
5. is / he / 20
6. they / 18 / are
7. live / Park Street / I / on
activities.answerSummary:
1. I am Sam.
2. She is from a small town.
3. What is your name?
4. How old are you?
5. He is 20.
6. They are 18.
7. I live on Park Street.
Number 4: How old are you? Not How old you are?
6 or 7 right: good.
5 or less: read Patterns 1 and 3 and do it again.
activities.soloPath: Write each sentence. Read it out loud. Check with the key.

assignments.title: Hello, my name is …
assignments.instructions:
Two parts.
1. Tap the mic. Say hello. Say your name and spell it. Say how old you are and where you are from. Say goodbye.
2. Write a library card like Writing 4, in capital letters.
You can use a made-up name, age and place.

teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
teacherNotes.note: Everything here is built for a learner with nobody beside them: every card has a worked example before its practice, every exercise has a key with a score line, and every speaking task ends with record, listen back and a visible checklist. If you are helping, listen to the recordings together rather than correcting mid-sentence.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
teacherNotes.noteType: The one error worth your attention
teacherNotes.note: Dropping the verb be: I Ana, She from a small town. For learners whose language needs no word there, these feel complete and correct. Treat it as a difference between languages, not carelessness. It usually settles within a few units if it is noticed every time, gently.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
teacherNotes.note: Numbers stop at 20 in this unit; 21 to 100 come in Unit 9. An adult therefore cannot yet say a true age, and every task says a made-up age is fine. Never push for a real age and never correct a made-up one.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
teacherNotes.noteType: A fixed phrase, not a pattern
teacherNotes.note: Where do you live? is used as a fixed phrase to understand and answer, because live is taught here. Questions with do and does are Unit 7's pattern: do not explain do in this unit. Likewise the plurals in the number sentences (two pens) are used, not taught; plural -s is Unit 2.

teacherNotes.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01
teacherNotes.sourceFile: Grade 1 Unit 1; Grade 2 Unit 1; Grade 3 Unit 1
teacherNotes.note: The AI tutor is a rehearsal partner, not a marking service, and no task is scored by it alone. The learner is told throughout that a made-up name, age and place are fine. Keep that wording, and never ask the learner to give the tutor real personal details.
